subject: Tenant geofence & operator identity pack — CAIQ/SIG evidence request
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@medicuslabs.com>

Cc: Legal - Medicus Labs <legal@medicuslabs.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2027 08:14:00 -0500
Subject: Tenant geofence & operator identity pack — initial ask

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call last week. Medicus is preparing our SIG/CAIQ packet and the compliance team has a few specific asks related to the ‘tenant geofence’ controls and operator identity for private deployments:

- A roster of on-call operator identities (name + role + corporate email) who can access EU-only VPC nodes for our account.
- Evidence that operator access is tied to corporate SSO + 2FA and time-limited elevated sessions (audit timestamps).
- Network topology showing private link endpoints, NAT/egress paths, and any cross-region peering (diagram or SVG preferred).
- SOC 2 artifact id references for retention and log shipping for EU nodes (we'll map these to our evidence tracker).

Can you provide a consolidated packet or point me to a drive folder? We’re aiming to close this portion of the assessment by Dec 18 so quick turnaround appreciated.

Thanks,
Samira

Subject: Re: Tenant geofence & operator identity pack — initial ask

Hi Samira —

Appreciate the clear list. We can do a consolidated packet. Quick notes up-front so expectations are aligned:

- Operator roster: we can provide a CSV export that includes names, roles (on-call / operator / SRE), corporate email, and the operator badge ID used for audit trails. For privacy we substitute personal phone numbers with corporate contact points.
- Access controls: Redwood enforces SSO (SAML/OIDC) + 2FA by default. For private deployments we enforce just-in-time (JIT) elevation via our internal bastion with sessions recorded. We will include sample audit timestamps (redacted) showing JIT sessions and a pointer to the retention policy.
- Network diagram: attaching a topology SVG (privatelink_topology.svg) showing EU-only endpoints and the explicit egress path to our EU audit collector. Note there is a documented fallback to a cross-region tiered model for burst failover — we'll label that as “failover lane” in the diagram.
- SOC 2 artifacts: we will provide an index mapping Redwood SOC 2 artifact IDs to the specific retention and log shipping claims for EU nodes (soc2-artifact-index.tsv).

I’m looping in Marissa (Legal & Compliance lead on Private) and Ben (Ops lead for EU private deployments) to add any service-level notes and the operator roster CSV. Expect a consolidated drive folder by end of day.

Action items:
- Marissa: please confirm if we should include the full operator emails or masked variants for the roster.
- Ben: please attach the CSV export and 1–2 redacted JIT session records.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Principal Security PM, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

- operator_roster_v2.csv (columns: operator_name, role, corporate_email, badge_id, primary_oncall=true/false)
- soc2-artifact-index.tsv (maps SOC 2 control IDs to our retention/collection artifacts)
- two redacted JIT session records (audit_timestamps_20271130.log / audit_timestamps_20271205.log)
- privatelink_topology.svg (diagram of EU private endpoints + labeled failover lane)

Notes / clarifications:
- The operator CSV contains full corporate emails; if Medicus requires masked emails for sharing to external recipients, we can produce a masked variant ('operator_roster_v2_masked.csv') with emails replaced by token@redwood.internal and provide access controls on the drive. Please advise which you prefer.
- The SOC 2 artifact index references our internal evidence ids. If you want the underlying artifacts, we will require a customer NDA addendum (standard for SOC artifact exports to third parties). Let us know if Medicus Legal wants that.
- Regarding cross-region peering: the diagram shows a labeled 'failover lane' that can be exercised only under capacity/latency incidents per our routing policy. This is a documented behavior in our Private deployment runbook.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cEvidencePack

If everything looks good, we can drop in the masked CSV and the two redacted audit logs into the folder and set view-only.
